# VIGAT

**VIGAT: VLM-guided gene activity quantification from single-cell
ATAC-seq**

VIGAT uses a vision-language model (VLM) to read TSS-centered
single-cell ATAC coverage plots and select, for each marker gene, one
compact genomic window that best captures its cluster-specific chromatin
accessibility. The selected regions are then used to quantify ATAC
fragments and construct a gene-by-cell activity matrix. VIGAT relies
only on unsupervised ATAC clusters and does not require explicit cell
type annotations.

![](reference/figures/vigat_example.png)  
*The window VIGAT selects (blue) on a TSS-centered ATAC coverage plot of
a human islet sample.*

## Installation

VIGAT needs R (\>= 4.2). Install the Bioconductor and CRAN dependencies
first, then install VIGAT from GitHub:

``` r
install.packages(c("Seurat", "Signac", "remotes"))
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("GenomicRanges", "GenomeInfoDb", "IRanges", "S4Vectors", "BiocGenerics"))

remotes::install_github("beijie02/VIGAT")
```

## Quick start

VIGAT sends coverage plots to the OpenAI API, so you need your own
OpenAI API key ([create one here](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys);
API usage is billed to your OpenAI account).

``` r
# IMPORTANT! Assign your OpenAI API key. See the vignette for details
Sys.setenv(OPENAI_API_KEY = "your_openai_API_key")

library(VIGAT)
library(Signac)
library(Seurat)

# obj: a processed Signac Seurat object with an "ATAC" assay,
#      gene annotation and fragment files.
res <- VIGAT(
  obj         = obj,
  genes       = c("INS", "GCG", "SST", "PRSS1", "PECAM1", "LUM"),
  tissue      = "Islet",
  cluster_col = "ATAC_cluster"   # metadata column with ATAC clusters; NULL uses Idents(obj)
)

res$vigat_windows        # GRanges: one selected window per gene
res$count_matrix         # gene x cell ATAC counts in those windows

# Add the counts as a new assay for downstream analysis
obj[["VIGAT"]] <- CreateAssayObject(counts = res$count_matrix)
```

[`Sys.setenv()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.setenv.html) sets the key
for the current R session. To set it permanently, add
`OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_API_key` to `~/.Renviron`
([`usethis::edit_r_environ()`](https://usethis.r-lib.org/reference/edit.html)
opens it) and restart R.

### ⚠️ Warning: avoid sharing your API key with others or uploading it to public spaces.

Do not write the key into scripts you share, and do not commit
`.Renviron` to GitHub.

## Output

[`VIGAT()`](https://beijie02.github.io/VIGAT/reference/VIGAT.md) writes
nothing to disk. It returns a list:

| Element | Description |
|----|----|
| `vigat_windows` | `GRanges` with the selected window for each gene |
| `vigat_window_df` | The same windows as a data frame (gene, chr, start, end, width) |
| `count_matrix` | Sparse gene-by-cell fragment counts in the windows |
| `diagnostics` | Raw model response, genes found and genes skipped |
| `intermediates` | With `return_intermediates = TRUE`: TSS info, overlapping peaks, the coverage plots sent to the model, the prompt, the full API response and run information |
| `highlighted_plots` | With `return_highlighted_plots = TRUE`: one ggplot per gene with the selected window highlighted |

Save anything you need with the usual R functions, for example:

``` r
res <- VIGAT(obj, genes = marker_genes, tissue = "Islet",
             return_highlighted_plots = TRUE)
write.csv(res$vigat_window_df, "vigat_windows.csv", row.names = FALSE)
for (g in names(res$highlighted_plots)) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(paste0(g, "_vigat.png"), res$highlighted_plots[[g]],
                  width = 7, height = 7, dpi = 150)
}
```

## Vignette

A full walkthrough on an example human islet dataset: [Getting started
with VIGAT](https://beijie02.github.io/VIGAT/articles/VIGAT.html)

The example data (Signac object, fragment file and index) are available
on Zenodo:
[doi:10.5281/zenodo.23347228](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23347228).

## Main arguments

| Argument | Default | Description |
|----|----|----|
| `obj` | (required) | Signac Seurat object with an `ATAC` assay, gene annotation and fragment files |
| `genes` | (required) | Marker genes to score |
| `tissue` | (required) | Tissue name given to the model as context, e.g. `"Islet"` |
| `species` | `"human"` | Species given to the model; `NULL` omits it |
| `cluster_col` | `NULL` | Metadata column with ATAC clusters; `NULL` uses `Idents(obj)` |
| `min_atac_cluster_cells` | `50` | Clusters with fewer cells are removed before plotting |
| `openai_model` | `"gpt-5.5"` | OpenAI model that reads the plots |
| `return_intermediates` | `FALSE` | Also return TSS info, peaks, input coverage plots, prompt and API logs |
| `return_highlighted_plots` | `FALSE` | Also return one coverage plot per gene with the selected window highlighted |

## Troubleshooting

- **`OPENAI_API_KEY is not set`**: set it with
  [`Sys.setenv()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Sys.setenv.html) or add
  `OPENAI_API_KEY=...` to `~/.Renviron`.
- **Error in the count-matrix step**: `Fragments(obj)` must point to
  fragment files that exist on the machine running VIGAT.
- **Gene skipped**: the gene is missing from the ATAC annotation, or its
  chromosome is absent from the peak set. Check
  `res$diagnostics$genes_skipped`.
- **PDF too large**: OpenAI limits uploads to 50 MB. Use fewer genes per
  run.
